summary: The wizard’s “blank scroll” wish is a valid unlabeled-object qualifier in C: readobjnam() resolves it to SCR_BLANK_PAPER and returns the object. JavaScript currently rejects the parsed unlabeled flag before its existing blank-scroll lookup branch, so the wish aborts before the following marker-writing commands run.

source.branch: In wizard mode, a Ctrl-W wish of “blank scroll” leaves d.unlabeled set after preparse and d.bp ending in “scroll”. C readobjnam_postparse1() resolves that qualifier to SCR_BLANK_PAPER and continues to typfnd; it is a valid object result, not an unmatched wish or a write.c:dowrite failure.
callers: cmd.c:2001 routes the wizard wish command to wizcmds.c:wiz_wish(); wiz_wish() at wizcmds.c:32-44 calls zap.c:makewish() at line 38.

zap.c:makewish() at zap.c:6314-6422 obtains the wish string and calls readobjnam() at 6360. It uses the returned object for the wish and only prints the no-match message and retries when readobjnam() returns null at 6361-6364.
dependencies: Preserve readobjnam()’s object return through zap.c:makewish(): a successfully resolved blank scroll proceeds to the returned-object path, while only null enters makewish()’s retry branch. The current JS qualifier refusal throws before that contract can run.

evidence: Saved queue entry synthetic/v6/wizard-write-marker-scroll is from challenges/manifests/v6.json (SHA-256 7523b91e823f4e3906c9acdc9a3d80f8469c27c2caab8fc8fbd6967dbfdcab5f) and challenges/cases/v6/wizard-write-marker-scroll.session.json (SHA-256 e8f78b1b83cf79ac36cd10644ca8004c5cc3237b94a333112f297c20ed16231c). Its saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260926071400-v6.json was examined at 3b1e337022043d314860fa14efc520d2600bf194: 28/51 screens and cursors, 2454/2462 RNG calls, 23 screens remaining; first mismatch is a stop at step 28 with “a wish that sets unlabeled”.

The prepared recipe challenges/cases/v6/wizard-write-marker-scroll.recipe.session.json uses Ctrl-W “magic marker”, then Ctrl-W “blank scroll”, followed by an apply/write sequence. In the C recording, step 28 accepts “blank scroll” and displays “p - an unlabeled scroll”; its RNG includes next_ident(mkobj.c:521), blessorcurse(mkobj.c:1846), and makewish(zap.c:6421), showing C created and returned the wished object before the later writing prompt.

Upstream objnam.c:3933-3960 initializes d.unlabeled to 0; objnam.c:4029-4033 treats “blank ”, “unlabeled ”, and “unlabelled ” as synonymous and sets it to 1. objnam.c:4514-4516 then recognizes the scroll suffix, sets d.typ = SCR_BLANK_PAPER, and returns the typfnd action.

Upstream objnam.c:4914-4944 runs preparse and the lookup chain; objnam.c:5037 creates the selected object. The active production caller is zap.c:6360-6364, where a returned object continues the wish while only null prints “Nothing fitting that description exists in the game.” and retries.

In JS, objnam_readobjnam.js:1128-1131 parses “blank ” into d.unlabeled, and the matching C branch already exists at js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1508-1514. However, js/objnam_readobjnam.js:1870-1895 lists unlabeled as unsupported and readobjnam_lookup() calls requireSimpleWishQualifiers() at 2037 before it calls readobjnam_postparse1() at 2039. That guard order creates the step-28 stop before the existing resolver can return SCR_BLANK_PAPER.
